context.text: Birthday Collision Simulator A data science club is developing a Python program to demonstrate the Birthday Paradox, which shows that in a surprisingly small group of people, two individuals are likely to share the same birthday. Since collecting real birthday data is impractical, the program randomly generates birthdays for 50 people. It first generates a random year, month, and day while ensuring that the generated date is valid by checking whether the selected year is a leap year. The birthdays are stored as datetime.date objects and then converted into their corresponding day of the year (1–365 or 366), since only the day and month are relevant for detecting birthday matches. These values are stored in a list, sorted in ascending order, and scanned for repeated values. Each repeated value represents a birthday collision. Because the birthdays are generated randomly, running the program multiple times produces different numbers of collisions, helping students understand the Birthday Paradox through simulation.
